reviews.review: I play with potato settings. The game looks beautiful still. The gun-play is good, the music is stellar. And the lore. Oh my god the lore. And all of it voiced with amazing voice actors! Of the 23 hours (at this time) of playing, I haven't even scraped the surface. The game has a level of detail that feels refreshing, almost overwhelming. There are moments where I think, "this game has no right being this good". Right now, I have a solo Hunter/Gunslinger character, and a character I play with friends as a support Medic/Alchemist role, and both are thoroughly enjoyable. I don't know the budget for the game, or the history of the franchise/developers, but I can say that it was money well spent. I would definitely recommend for casual players and hardcore players alike.
Good Game. Will Run, Roll, Shoot and die again.
At first I wasn't to convince for this game, but now I can't stop playing it

Coop recommend, if it's on a deep sale. Review is for base game. Played through this twice in coop.

I actually may have preferred the first game, considering that enemies sometimes flanked you there by spawning behind and areas felt more varied. But maybe that is bias.


+ Large variety of accessories/weapons
+ Boss variety
+ Replay value, you're expected to do so a few times, since the areas are randomised to an extent


* You don't really need the new weapons or weapon abilities etc. you can just use what you have at the beginning to beat the game, which can be considered good or bad
* Lore, like in the first game, is not really that interesting to me, but it's there


- Armor is rare to find and doesn't change much apart from weight and armor rating
- Accessories, while plentiful, offer only minor effects most of the time
- Some secrets are so obscure you will likely never find them without a guide (not that you need to find them)
- Certain attacks, like with final boss, are hard to understand how to avoid


I would not recommend full price as one playthrough doesn't take that long and while there's replay value, RNG means you might bump into same area layouts/bosses. Still, you could do worse if it's on a hefty sale.
